newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's DEKA plans to become more international.
newsitem.headline: Germany's DEKA plans to become more international.

text.p: Deka, the fund management wing of the German savings bank organisation, said on Wednesday that it plans to meet its customers' needs for international investments by a number of cooperation agreements.

Gustav Adolf Schroeder, management board chairman of Deka, said in an interview with the group's in-house publication Info, that the savings bank group had to become more internationally oriented to secure long-term success.

Schroeder said he was confident that Deka's discussions with a "global player" in the investment research and fund management area, as well as negotiations with a Swiss private bank in the area of asset management, would be successful.
He said that a decision by Deka to set up in Dublin from the middle of this year also gave the group a valuable foothold in the "anglo-saxon" area.
